clue.text: Broadcast travels over island

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the words that follow are to be judged by their sound

parts.note: travels is 'goes', and over is O, the cricket abbreviation

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin about journeys out to some island.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, GOES O runs together as GOZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gozo is the second largest island of the Maltese archipelago, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: To make likely trouble for oneself, demand sex

definitions.text: To make likely trouble for oneself

parts.note: to demand is to request something insistently
'it' is a familiar euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Warning that anyone who demands sex is courting trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes behaving in a way that invites the punishment or trouble one then receives.

clue.text: Medic works on variable accumulation of fluid

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
OPS is short for opuses, musical works
in algebra x, y and z are standard variables

explanation.surface: A doctor doing research on a changeable build-up of fluid in a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old medical name for oedema, a swelling caused by excess watery fluid collecting in tissue.

clue.text: Strong drink, as second child sleeps soundly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
CH is the standard abbreviation for child

indicators.note: soundly is read as 'by sound', so the last word is to be spelt by how it is pronounced

parts.note: sleeps are naps, and the same sound is spelt here with a double consonant

explanation.surface: A strong drink knocks back the parent while the younger child sleeps deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: Soundly looks like it describes deep sleep; it tells you that naps only has to sound right, not be spelt right.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled spirit from Germany and Scandinavia, so it is a strong drink.

clue.text: Former banker revealing all?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... family's bank, ..., collapsed in 1995
second meaning: uncovering, as in stripping to show everything

explanation.walkthrough: Barings was an old London merchant bank founded by the Baring family; it collapsed after the Nick Leeson trading scandal. The question mark covers the pun on a banker stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Baring family were famous bankers, and baring means uncovering or exposing to view.

clue.text: Youngsters greeting old fellow

parts.note: yo is an informal greeting
O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Kids calling out hello to an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoof is a jokey British spelling of 'youth', mimicking street pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is slang for young people collectively, so it stands for teenagers and other youngsters.

clue.text: Partner going against type

parts.note: con as in pros and cons means against
a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: A spouse who is not the kind you would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, especially the wife or husband of a reigning monarch.

clue.text: No cat flaps? In which case, go figure!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form a case, and the next word goes inside it
flaps suggests letters fluttering about out of order, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An absent cat, a flap with nothing coming through, and a shrug of 'go figure!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go figure!' reads as a slangy shrug; split it, and go is the inserted piece while figure is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided plane shape, and a geometric shape is a figure.

clue.text: Swell until very loud

parts.note: until and to both mark an end point, as in nine till five
ff is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Something growing in volume until it is deafening.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell looks like a verb about sound growing; here it is the noun for a smart, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is old slang for a fashionable gentleman, and a toff is a British word for a posh person.

clue.text: One starting a suit design outside No. 4 in Savile Row

indicators.note: one word is placed outside, wrapping round, the selected letter

parts.note: a design is a plan

indicators.note: number four in a word is its fourth letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the fourth letter of this word
a row is a quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: A tailor beginning a bespoke suit in Savile Row, London's famous street of tailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a lawsuit, not clothing; Savile Row and design all push towards tailoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the person who brings a case, or suit, against another in a civil court.

clue.text: Nameless troll again upset Daisy?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation for name is removed from the letters

parts.note: taken as written; its N is the one removed

explanation.surface: An anonymous internet troll who is upset once more about someone called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name. The question mark warns that Daisy is just one example of a creature's pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a definition by example: Daisy is offered as the kind of name a pet or zoo reptile might carry.

clue.text: Black and blue?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Black and blue' suggests bruising, but the two colours are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something filthy with grime is black, and a blue joke is an obscene, smutty one; both are this word.

clue.text: City in Serbia — Budapest's to the North

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading the letters upwards, from bottom to top
the answer sits within the run of words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first name and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A geography note placing a Serbian city south of the Hungarian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The two European capitals are camouflage; the city is in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is the largest city of the United Arab Emirates, a major Gulf port and business centre.

clue.text: Girl with a mop edited today's puzzle? One row leads to another just the same

indicators.note: something edited has been reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner's puzzle being edited, followed by a remark about rows that repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Not one answer in this grid contains the letter E, so the whole crossword is a lipogram. The closing sentence appears to be a separate note in the source and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipogram is writing that deliberately avoids one letter, and this crossword avoids E throughout.

clue.text: Posh name for a president

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the maiden surname of Victoria Beckham, Posh Spice of the Spice Girls
second meaning: John ... or John Quincy ..., US presidents

explanation.walkthrough: Posh looks like an adjective for a grand name; it is Posh Spice, the pop singer born Victoria Adams.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Beckham's family surname matches that of two early American heads of state, father and son.

clue.text: Sit next to a bar

parts.note: taken as written
bar and but both mean except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Taking a seat beside a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border or lie directly alongside something, as one building adjoins another.

clue.text: Store ship close to docks

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Keeping a vessel near the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Store looks like a verb; it is a noun, the British catalogue retailer Argos.
explanation.definitionFit: Argos is a chain of British high-street shops selling goods from a catalogue, so it is a store.

clue.text: Friend wearing a nun's outfit docked in the capital

indicators.note: a person wearing an outfit is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a nun's robe is her habit
bud is American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A pal dressed as a nun turns up at the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates, so it is the capital named.

clue.text: Pakistan's opening bowler, perhaps getting fine

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word
a bowler is a kind of hat, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Pakistan's opening bowler doing well in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is a decoy: the bowler is a round-crowned hat, and opening only picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Phat is hip-hop slang meaning excellent or great, a sense close to fine as an approving word.

clue.text: Turn nose up at housework over and over again

indicators.note: over and over again means repeated, so the reversed piece appears twice
over means turned over, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: house gives HO, its abbreviation, and work gives OP, short for opus

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at doing chores time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: HO (house) plus OP (work) is reversed by 'over' to POOH, and 'and over again' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something contemptuously is to scorn it, as if snorting at it, which is to turn one's nose up.

clue.text: Daughter to topless peer: "That's a bit off!"

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a viscount is a rank of peer in the British nobility

explanation.surface: A daughter scolding a bare-chested aristocrat that his behaviour is not quite acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit off' sounds like disapproval; read literally it means a little taken off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a reduction in price, literally a bit knocked off what is charged.

clue.text: Short, lofted shot landing 25? Almost blush

indicators.note: landing in a place, the shot goes inside it; the IN of the cross-reference also signals the insertion
cut short, the shot loses its last letter

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, read as a location for the shot to land in

indicators.note: almost all of the court is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a lob is a shot hit high into the air, as in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player's mishit lob dropping into court, followed by a near-blush of embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 answer is IN COURT, so the shot lands in the court: trim each and put one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour is to go red in the face, which is what blushing means.

clue.text: Rifles motion rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: a motion is a bowel movement, a stool

explanation.surface: A proposal at a meeting about firearms is voted down.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion looks like a formal proposal; it is the medical sense of a bowel movement. Rifles is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a place is to search it to steal, so rifles means plunders or loots.

clue.text: Down wrong in record

indicators.note: one piece is placed in, inside, the other

parts.note: a log is a written record
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A mistake entered on the record, leaving someone feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is down is behind on points, which is to be losing the match.

clue.text: Fish and chips, cooked with lard

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and mixed, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: fish and chips fried in lard, the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips reads as a single dish; split it, and fish alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilchards are small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Working girl with bit sticking out at front

parts.note: pro is slang for a prostitute
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A prostitute with a protruding feature up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A prow is the pointed forward part of a ship, the part that projects at the front.

clue.text: Man with soft beard

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A fellow sporting a wispy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: Man looks like any male; it is a chess piece, as in chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the pawn is the lowliest of them.

clue.text: Growth of conflict over time

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: How a war grows and escalates over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A wart is a small hard lump on the skin, a kind of growth.

clue.text: Detective tailed a saint

indicators.note: to tail something is to remove its tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Columbo is the rumpled TV detective played by Peter Falk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective shadowing a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailed looks like following a suspect, which a detective would do; it means docked of its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: St Columba was the sixth-century Irish missionary who founded the monastery on Iona.

clue.text: Outcome of ruction, turning up here?

definitions.text: Outcome of ruction, turning up here?

indicators.note: an outcome is what a thing turns into, so the word that follows is turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Where a brawler ends up after a fight: before the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruction is a noisy row or brawl. The whole clue also describes the answer: after a ruction, you may find yourself appearing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose rowdy fight leads to charges ends up appearing before a judge, standing in court.
